skill.name: content-system-product-proposal
skill.title: Product proposal
skill.description: Argues, with evidence, why one product solution is the best, so the product owner can review, comment and decide before anything is built.

purpose: The single entry point for one Agnes feature through its whole life: argue and decide it before anything is built, then carry the plan, the progress, acceptance, feedback and lessons in the same document, so the owner, a teammate or an agent can pick it up at any point.
when_to_use: A new Agnes capability or a change to one: from the proposal the product owner reviews, through the build, to acceptance and later changes. One feature, one artifact, new versions only.
when_not_to_use: A bug fix, a data report (data-report) or a runbook.

method.instruction: Who has the problem, what they do today, what it costs, one real example with its source.
Read the code, docs and running app. Every claim gets a file path or link. Label what you could not inspect.
Read how 3 to 5 competitors solve it, from their own docs. Link each source.
At least two alternatives, including doing nothing, on the same criteria.
Have GPT Astra review the draft; address or rebut every finding.
Re-read PR, deploy, switch and test state from their sources at session start, before each publish and at session end; only then move 'last reconciled'.

lead.guidance: At most 3 sentences: what the feature is, where it stands now, and what the owner must decide or do next.

sections.title: What changed
sections.answers: What differs from the previous version, and why?
sections.guidance: Only this version against the previous one, each change with its reason and the comment or event it answers. Older history lives in the version notes and the Log.

sections.title: Summary
sections.answers: What is the feature, for whom, and why?
sections.guidance: 3 to 6 bullets a newcomer understands: what users get, how it works, under which switch and where it is on. Link the decision register; never repeat it.

sections.title: Status now
sections.answers: Where is it, what waits for whom, and how fresh is this?
sections.guidance: Focus in one sentence. Four separate states: code merged, deployed (where), enabled (which switches, where), accepted (who, when), each with how it was verified. Three times: last work event, last reconciled with sources, next check (marked so the page flags it when overdue). Waiting for you (decisions, reviews, approvals) and waiting for others (what, who, since when). A links row: Linear, GitHub PRs, related artifacts, user docs. Before the build: stage Proposal and the decisions needed by when.

sections.title: Continue here
sections.answers: What does the next person or agent need to carry on?
sections.guidance: Active slice, branch and PR with its state as gh reports it, last verified result, next action, blockers, where the work lives (session, worktree), responsible person. Rewritten whenever work stops or is handed over.

sections.title: What it does today
sections.answers: What can a user do now, step by step, and what are the limits?
sections.guidance: The current behaviour contract: numbered steps in the product's own words, then Limits (what does not work or was not tried live). Kept true; a change of scope, authority or guarantee goes through the decision register. Link the user docs page.

sections.title: Plan and progress
sections.answers: How is it built, in which order, and how far along is it?
sections.guidance: One slice table is the single source: permanent ID (W01...), alias, phase, what a user gets, state, PR link, opened, merged, note. The timeline is generated from it with a snapshot stamp, never drawn by hand. Phases with ambitious dates at AI-agent build speed (days), none waiting for decisions; the switch; dependencies; Waiting for others; Before production (including owed reviews); risks; given/when/then acceptance examples. A re-plan is a Log entry; the original plan stays as a collapsed record.

sections.title: Acceptance and feedback
sections.answers: Has the owner accepted it, what was verified, and what is still open?
sections.guidance: Verdict (who, when, on which deployment, with which reservations) or 'none yet'. A link to the E2E acceptance plan artifact; detailed results live there. A table of what was verified where, with result, date and source. Feedback register: item, from, when, state, link. Known issues.

sections.title: Decisions
sections.answers: What has been decided, what is open, and why?
sections.guidance: One register of every decision, big and small (also simplifications and process rules): ID, question, decision, when, who, state (open, decided, deferred, amended by X, superseded by X), source. Open decision cards follow in full as meeting briefs: what it is about (today, what changes, why now); one example shown in every option; options table with Pros, Cons, Change later, Who does this (sourced); recommendation with its reason; a form. Decided cards are collapsed records. No decision lives only in chat or agent memory.

sections.title: The problem
sections.answers: Who is hurt, how, and what does it cost today?
sections.guidance: Who, situation, cost in numbers, one real example with source (ticket, Slack thread, session).

sections.title: Goals and non-goals
sections.answers: What must change, and what is out of scope?
sections.guidance: Goals as user outcomes; non-goals explicit so silence promises nothing.

sections.title: Principles
sections.answers: Which rules must the solution respect?
sections.guidance: 3 to 6 rules, each with a short name and one plain line; refer to them by name, never by number.

sections.title: How we know it worked
sections.answers: Which numbers prove success, and what was measured?
sections.guidance: Outcome checks a user would notice: baseline (before the build), target, date, measured value with when and evidence (or 'not measured' / 'blocked'); guardrails that must not get worse.

sections.title: Current state in Agnes
sections.answers: How does it work today, for users and in code?
sections.guidance: Before the build: the user flow today, a code map (repo paths), annotated screenshots of the real app. Once the build starts, title it 'Baseline before the build' with its commit and date and point to What it does today.

sections.title: Research and competition
sections.answers: How do others solve it, and where is Agnes?
sections.guidance: Competitors' approaches, a comparison table, Agnes now vs after each phase; every claim linked.

sections.title: Proposal
sections.answers: What will users do and see?
sections.guidance: User journey, behaviour, states, limits, errors; mockups labelled Concept.

sections.title: Alternatives and why this one
sections.answers: Why is this option better than the others?
sections.guidance: Do nothing plus at least one real option, same criteria, argued verdict.

sections.title: Architecture impact
sections.answers: Which parts of Agnes change?
sections.guidance: C4 containers and components touched, a diagram, and a surfaces matrix (Tests, Docs, Frontend, API, CLI, MCP, external services) with yes/no and why.

sections.title: Retro
sections.answers: What worked and what did not in how agents built it, and what do we change?
sections.guidance: After each phase and after acceptance: what worked, what did not (stalls, repeated failures, review loops, usage limits, manual rescues), each backed by the Log or a named source; then a table of changes to skills, hooks, checks, rules or templates with state (proposed, in place) and link.

sections.title: Log
sections.answers: What happened when?
sections.guidance: Append-only, newest first, times with timezone: type (PR opened, merged, CI failure, incident, fix, finding, re-plan, decision, blocker, deploy), one line, link. A failure links to its fix; repeated identical failures are one entry with a count. Generated from GitHub and the version history where possible; raw output stays in CI. Missing history is marked 'not recorded', never reconstructed. Collapsed.

sections.title: Second opinion
sections.answers: What did GPT Astra find, and what was done?
sections.guidance: Each round with its date and what it reviewed; each finding with its resolution: changed (where) or rebutted (why). Per-slice reviews may stay in PRs; unresolved findings are listed here.

sections.title: Glossary
sections.answers: What do the new or redefined terms mean?
sections.guidance: Every new or redefined term, matching GLOSSARY.md.

sections.title: Sources
sections.answers: What backs the claims?
sections.guidance: Numbered list: title, link or repo path, date or commit; only what was actually read.

sections.title: Appendix: technical detail
sections.answers: What detail supports the text without changing it?
sections.guidance: Collapsible: data models, API shapes, raw research notes.

hierarchy: Summary and Status now carry the document; open decisions and the next action must be findable without scrolling through history. Decided cards, the original plan and the log are collapsed records. Detail goes to the appendix; decisive caveats stay in the main text.

rules: Bilingual Czech and English, Czech first, for the lead, summary, status, current behaviour, plan text, acceptance verdict, decision cards, retro and design sections. The slice table, the registers and the log are English only and shown in both language views.
Plain words, short sentences. Numbers over adjectives.
Explain every number, unit and term on first use (what 180 s measures, what a turn is); no slogans or abstract policy wording.
Every claim about Agnes cites a repo path or link; every claim about a competitor cites a source link.
Mark each consequential claim verified, inferred or unverified.
No word limits: say what the reader needs, nothing more. No AI slop and no filler; data the document needs belongs in it.
Report a state literally as its owning tool reports it (OPEN, MERGED, AUTO-MERGE ENABLED) with the time it was read; never carry a state over from an earlier version without re-reading it.
Label every mockup or generated image Concept.
Every commitment names an owner (default: the requester) and a date.
No filler, no hype, no empty section. Every sentence changes what the reader knows or decides.
Each visual has a takeaway caption and a text equivalent; never colour alone.

visuals: Annotated screenshots of today, a competitor comparison table, a C4 diagram of what changes, and a progress timeline generated from the slice table with a snapshot stamp.
checklist: Lead: what the feature is, where it stands, what the owner must do next.
Status now shows four states, three times and a next check the page flags when overdue.
Every state in Status now and Continue here was re-read from its source for this version.
One slice table; the timeline is generated from it in the same snapshot.
Every decision is a register row; decided cards are collapsed; nothing contradicts a later decision.
The problem has one real example with a source.
Each metric has a baseline, a target, a date and a measured value or 'not measured'.
Every Agnes claim has a path or link; every competitor claim a source; every PR number is a link.
At least two alternatives, including doing nothing.
Each open decision card follows the meeting-brief structure and has a form.
The surfaces matrix covers Tests, Docs, Frontend, API, CLI, MCP and external services.
A rollout switch and given/when/then acceptance examples.
Related artifacts (polls, E2E plan) are linked both ways and their outcome is recorded here.
Every Astra finding is addressed or rebutted.
Czech and English say the same thing.

variants.title: Building or built
variants.when: Work on the feature has started (the first PR is open); stays for the rest of its life.
